thread:
maya.ops: Heads-up — since the gpu-operator rollout last night i'm seeing a spike in GPU pod evictions in eu-west. node messages show driver/CUDA mismatches and device plugin re-registration loops.

ben.eng: saw this too, around 23:40 UTC. pods moved to other zones and a few apps hit OOM/latency. any quick mitigation?

ravi.enginfra: logs from node-12: 
```
Jun 10 23:41:02 node-12 kubelet: device plugin: /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: handshake failed: driver version mismatch
Jun 10 23:41:03 node-12 kernel: nvidia: module tainted, version 520.61 -> expected 520.78
```

sasha.ml: that kernel-module mismatch smells like a driver build vs kernel headers miscompile. did the operator upgrade include a node image or driver manager change?

maya.ops: gpu-operator v1.8.0 -> v1.9.0. changelog mentions device-plugin timing and advertise-before-probe behavior changed. suspect some nodes advertise GPUs before proprietary driver fully loaded. scheduler then binds GPU pods, kubelet later evicts.

ben.eng: consequence: pods are scheduled, init containers fail on /dev/nvidiactl, then kubelet evicts and reschedules. churn causes capacity to appear lower than actual -> backlog.

infra-sre-bot: Alert: GPU pod eviction rate increased 8x in eu-west in last 15m. Affected deployments: redwood-infer, batch-encoder, eval-worker.

ravi.enginfra: temporary mitigation: cordon the newest node pool (np-gpu-roll-2) and scale up the older stable pool. need approval to pause rollout.

ben.eng: +1 for pause and scale. also add a taint to nodes of np-gpu-roll-2 so scheduler won't bind until we confirm device plugin stable.

maya.ops: i'm going to open a rollback PR for the operator to v1.8.0 and start cordoning. can we collect a few more logs first? specifically device-plugin logs and dmesg for missing symbols.

sasha.ml: i'll grab a failing pod's init logs and NCCL logs (if present). NCCL errors look like: 
```
NCCL WARN Call to cudaLaunchKernel failed: %d
NCCL WARN cudaErrorInvalidDevice: invalid device ordinal
```

ravi.enginfra: also noticed kubelet reported allocatable GPUs as 0 briefly, then back to N. that's consistent with device-plugin flapping. Suggest adding a small readiness gate: device plugin should advertise only after probe passes.

ben.eng: workaround we can apply cluster-side: add a small mutating webhook patch to reject scheduling onto nodes labeled `gpu-roll=1` until we mark them `gpu-ready=true`. quick but hacky.

maya.ops: agreed hacky but safe. rollbacks + cordon + scale up old pool first. i'll push rollback and taint plan in 5.

deploy-bot: Deploy request submitted: rollback gpu-operator -> v1.8.0. CI checks passed. Will apply to eu-west canary pool first.

ravi.enginfra: long-term fix: update our node image pipeline to pin kernel-headers and nvidia-driver builds together. also request gpu-operator include a pre-probe wait-for-driver flag. i've opened infra#912 for that.

ben.eng: action items: (1) cordon np-gpu-roll-2 (maya), (2) scale up stable pool by +12 GPUs (ravi), (3) apply rollback to operator canary then region (deploy-bot), (4) collect triage logs and attach to infra#912 (sasha).

maya.ops: starting cordon and rollback now. will post statuses.

infra-sre-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-045 — gpu scheduling/eviction spike, impacted region eu-west, mitigation in progress.

ben.eng: after rollback we should run a small synthetic workload across a canary node for 30m to validate device-plugin stability and NCCL allreduce passes.

maya.ops: noted. planning 30m soak, will update thread when done.

sasha.ml: preliminary postmortem notes: driver-kernel ABI drift + operator timing change + lack of kubelet readiness gating = cascade. put evals in place to surface allocatable vs actual before full rollout.

ravi.enginfra: also cost note: the churn caused cross-zone reschedules and temporary double-scheduling on cpu nodes; should track billing delta, might be ~+3-5% for the window. logging that to finance.

maya.ops: rollback applied to canary. waiting 2m for pod restarts. will confirm if evictions stop.

deploy-bot: Rollback applied to canary: success. Monitoring shows device-plugin stable on canary node.

maya.ops: canary looks good. promoting rollback to eu-west. starting rollout now.

ben.eng: nice. after rollout, let's add a kubelet pre-start probe that checks for /dev/nvidia0 and driver module versions before marking node ready for GPUs.

maya.ops: added to infra#912. closing loop here when rollout completes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
